task: Add four opt-in live-provider smoke tests (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, raw fetch) to the llm-http-proxy package — one per provider, each gated by its own API-key env var (same opt-in pattern as the existing RUN_BENCH benchmark). Default `npm test` must keep passing fast and free of network/credential dependencies.

analysis.objective: Add four opt-in live-provider smoke tests (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, raw fetch) to the llm-http-proxy package, each gated by its own API-key env var so the default `npm test` stays fast and network-free, proving the in-process interceptor captures real LLM HTTP traffic.
analysis.successDefinition: Done and correct iff: (1) four new files exist in packages/llm-http-proxy/src/ named *.integration.test.ts, one per provider (anthropic, openai, gemini, fetch-baseline); (2) the package's default jest run (`npm test`) discovers all four `*.integration.test.ts` files but resolves each to `describe.skip` (zero test bodies execute) and the actual baseline of 126 package tests + 5 root tests (per horizon-6 completion record) stays green in its existing wall-clock time with zero network egress; (3) each new test is gated to skip when its corresponding API-key env var is unset (same opt-in pattern as RUN_BENCH=1), and prints a single skip line per missing key; (4) when all required env vars are set, running `npx jest src/<file>.integration.test.ts` per-provider makes exactly one small real completion call each, asserts the emitted LlmLogEntry carries provider-expected fields (model, tokens or non-empty body, url host), and passes; (5) `npm run build` and `npm run lint` remain green; (6) no API key value is ever logged, asserted, or written to a fixture.
assumptions: The package's default jest config matches the `*.test.ts` discovery rule (the same one RUN_BENCH=1 in src/benchmark.test.ts relies on) so that `*.integration.test.ts` is naturally excluded from `npm test` — Discovery will verify; if it is NOT excluded, the opt-in gate must be lifted to a describe.skip wrapper plus an `npm test` config tweak.

The four smoke tests can be discovered explicitly via `npx jest --testPathPattern=integration` (or direct file paths) without changing package.json scripts — i.e. an opt-in run mode exists without ceremony.

API-key env var names follow the obvious provider conventions (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY) and can be named in the test file without a prior package-level naming decision; the fetch baseline needs no env var.
`fetch` is a global in the package's supported Node version (it is — see package.json engines and prior horizons' use), so a raw-fetch baseline needs no shim.
The OTEL horizon-6 lazy `require()` pattern in src/otel.ts is irrelevant to these tests — they exercise the interceptor end-to-end via real HTTP, not via the Logger seam.

Each provider's smallest non-streaming completion call (a few input + few max-output tokens) returns within a reasonable per-test timeout (e.g. 30s) and costs fractions of a cent; one call per provider per opt-in run is the budget.

The horizon-5 RUN_BENCH pattern (`describe` gated by an env-var check that resolves to `describe.skip` when unset) is the literal template for these new tests — copy the shape, do not invent a new one.
risks: API-key leakage via the package's own redaction logic — if any captured log entry or its raw body accidentally contains the API key (e.g. via a malformed auth header that lands in the URL), the smoke test will print it. The test MUST redact-assert the entry and MUST never assert against the raw Authorization header value, and a hard rule that keys are read from process.env ONLY (no hardcoded fallbacks) is needed to keep keys off disk.

Default `npm test` regression: if the `*.integration.test.ts` suffix is picked up by jest's `testMatch` (Discovery must confirm it is NOT), the default gate will try to hit the live network — this horizon's success definition collapses. Mitigation: assert via the analysis output that the existing testMatch is unchanged and that `npm test` runs the same number of suites/tests as the recorded baseline (79 package tests).

Live-API flakiness / shape drift: providers change response shapes and rate limits. A smoke test that hardcodes a model name or response field may break on the next provider release. Mitigation: pin to a documented stable model per provider and assert on the minimal common field set (model, url host); avoid asserting on token counts since billing/limit drift can change those.

Cost amplification: each opt-in run that has all three keys set makes four paid calls. Without a separate per-test timeout or rate-limit guard, repeated runs in CI could add up. The opt-in gate is the only mitigation; this is acceptable per the user's one-smoke-per-provider scope but is recorded here.

Latency budget conflict: horizon-5's benchmark-results.md recorded a real-path p99 FAIL (177.6% of baseline) attributed to environmental noise. Adding live network tests to the same package does NOT exercise the benchmark path and does not heal that miss, but a careless implementer might accidentally couple them by reusing benchmark fixtures — keep them strictly separate.

Discoveries.md records that `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base@2.10.0` has no `addSpanProcessor()` (constructor-only). Not directly relevant to live tests, but if the live tests want to assert span emission via the OTEL Logger they will hit this — the live tests should NOT span-assert; just log-entry assert.

If a caller ever runs `npm test` in an environment where the `*.integration.test.ts` files ARE accidentally discovered (e.g. someone changes jest config), the network will be hit. The risk is silent because jest will not necessarily fail — it will just attempt to connect. Mitigation: keep an explicit test that proves `npm test` does NOT match `*.integration.test.ts`.

The horizon-5 decision pins OTEL posture as optional peer deps via the Logger seam. Live tests that exercise the interceptor against a real provider will NOT activate OTEL (peers absent in default install), which is correct — but this is recorded so an implementer does not try to add a wire OTEL collector assertion on top of the live smoke tests (that would mix two horizons' scope).

The Horizon-sizing checklist says a horizon is 3–5 phases; this objective's natural shape (one provider per phase, plus a fetch baseline, plus the gating harness) is 4–5 phases — at the upper edge of the cap. Risk: implementer bundles two providers into one phase to fit the count; the rubric must reject that (one provider per expectedResult).

There are no caller-supplied acceptance criteria that conflict with the security/correctness invariants (no secret-in-plaintext, no unbounded operation, no auth bypass) — the user's scope answers are compatible with all of them. Nothing to escalate.
outOfScope: Real `npm publish` — explicitly deferred by the user's redirect, not this horizon's job.
Semver-freeze decision for the public LlmLogEntry/LlmLoggingOptions surface — explicitly deferred by the user redirect.
ESM dist lazy-load verification (createRequire vs current emit) — explicitly deferred by the user redirect.
Consumer-facing OTEL docs in the package README — explicitly deferred by the user redirect.
Prepack/prepare auto-build so a fresh clone can publish — explicitly deferred by the user redirect.
Re-run of the recorded request-path p99 miss — explicitly deferred; the live tests do not exercise the bench path.
Streaming, auth-error, rate-limit, and retry coverage on each provider — user scoped to one smoke per provider; deeper coverage is a future horizon.
Wire-format OTLP/HTTP/gRPC collector export — horizon-6 closed the OTEL bar with InMemorySpanExporter; live tests must not reach for a real collector.
Trace propagation / context injection for spans — not in scope for live smoke tests.

New provider parsers (Mistral, Cohere, etc.) — the horizon-3 #9 collapse already removed the per-provider parser registry; these tests exercise the single defaultParser against real provider responses and require no parser changes.
Changing the public package API surface (index.ts exports) — these tests are internal to the package and must not add new exported symbols.
Modifying the root app or root tsconfig/jest config — package-local only, matching horizon-5/6's isolation discipline.
Hardcoded model-pinning past horizon — each test uses a small `string`-typed model id, no version-locking dependency.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is wiring opt-in smoke tests into a library's test harness — pure tooling/infrastructure work — and the project's decisions.md already classifies llm-http-proxy as technical at horizon-1.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A test that hits a real external service (here: live provider API); opt-in, never part of the default suite.
A runtime check that resolves to describe.skip when a precondition is missing (mirrors the RUN_BENCH=1 pattern in src/benchmark.test.ts).
One small real call asserting the interceptor captures expected fields end-to-end; not a full behavioral suite.
The env var name holding the credential for one provider (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY); never hardcoded.
The non-LLM raw fetch call used to prove interception fires on plain HTTPS regardless of provider-specific response shape.
The horizon-5 opt-in harness template in src/benchmark.test.ts; new integration tests copy its gate shape, not invent a new one.
How package.json's jest config picks up test files by glob; default must NOT match *.integration.test.ts.
Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini — each gets its own file and its own API-key env var; the baseline fetch is not a provider.
The bounded-context / subsystem name for the four *.integration.test.ts files added this horizon (fetch-baseline + anthropic + openai + gemini).

finding.finding: Verbatim from src/benchmark.test.ts: `const RUN_BENCH = process.env.RUN_BENCH === '1';` (line 317), then `if (RUN_BENCH) { describe('latency benchmark', benchmarkSuite); } else { describe.skip('latency benchmark (opt-in: RUN_BENCH=1)', benchmarkSuite); }` (lines 359-366). benchmarkSuite contains `test(...)` blocks with explicit timeouts (e.g. `}, 120000);` on lines 339, 356). The pattern uses EventEmitter + http.createServer for fakeReq and a real 127.0.0.1 server.
finding.implication: Replicate the if/else describe|describe.skip shape verbatim per test file (with the API-key presence check replacing the RUN_BENCH flag). Pass a 30-60s jest timeout per test.

finding.finding: No public `attachCapture` helper exists as a top-level helper — `attachCapture` is a public method on `Interceptor` (line 415 of interceptor.ts). Existing tests build a local `Interceptor`, pass `{ ...options, logger: (entry) => entries.push(entry) }` to collect entries (interceptor.test.ts lines 80-83), call `interceptor.install()`, run the code under test, await `new Promise((r) => setImmediate(r))` twice to flush deferred emissions, then `interceptor.restore()` (lines 84-90). A `withEntries` helper wraps this for reuse (lines 75-91).
finding.implication: Use `import { Interceptor } from './interceptor';` directly. Build the interceptor with `{ providers: [<provider host>], logger: (e) => entries.push(e) }`, install/restore, await two setImmediate ticks.

finding.finding: Defined in src/options.ts lines 18-31. Fields: `timestamp: Date`; `model: string`; `inputTokens: number`; `outputTokens: number`; `callerTrace: string`; `url: string`; optional `maskedRequestBody?`/`maskedResponseBody?` (capturePayloads-only); optional `error?`. Default config NEVER populates the masked-body fields.
finding.implication: Live tests assert on `model`, `url`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`. Avoid callerTrace (resolves to 'unknown' under Jest). capturePayloads stays default-off unless the test specifically needs body content.

finding.finding: No existing live-provider fixtures exist. OpenAI: POST `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with `{model:'gpt-4o-mini', messages:[{role:'user',content:'hi'}], max_tokens:1, stream:false}`. Anthropic: POST `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with `{model:'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022', max_tokens:1, messages:[...]}` plus headers `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `content-type: application/json`. Gemini: POST `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent?key=<key>` with `{contents:[{parts:[{text:'hi'}]}]}` (API key is a URL query parameter, not a header).
finding.implication: Each test must construct its provider's actual minimal body and endpoint. Gemini uses `?key=` query params; the key travels on the wire as part of the URL path, so the test MUST assert `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does not contain the key value.

finding.finding: Seven *.test.ts files under src/ (benchmark, event-stream-parser, interceptor, logger, otel, provider-parser, redaction). The horizon-6 ledger baseline reports 126 package tests + 5 root tests. `npx jest --listTests` returns exactly these 7 files.
finding.implication: Regression baseline is 126 package tests + 5 root tests in the same wall-clock time. After adding the 4 integration files, `npx jest --listTests` will return 11 files, but only the original 7 execute any test() bodies by default (the 4 new ones resolve to describe.skip when their env var is unset).

finding.finding: `engines.node` is `>=18`. `fetch` is a global in Node 18+ and routes through http.ClientRequest.prototype. No undici imports exist in the package.
finding.implication: The fetch baseline can use the global `fetch` directly with no shim.

finding.finding: `test`: `jest --passWithNoTests`; `lint`: `eslint "src/**/*.ts"`; `build`: `tsc -p tsconfig.cjs.json && tsc -p tsconfig.esm.json && npm run postbuild`; `typecheck`: `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`. The lint glob includes the new `*.integration.test.ts` files; tsc also includes src/ in tsconfig.json.
finding.implication: New files MUST pass eslint and typecheck (env-var strings need explicit `string | undefined` typing).

finding.finding: All existing test files import from internal src/ paths (`from './interceptor'`, `from './options'`, etc.), NEVER from the public entry point.
finding.implication: New integration tests must follow: `import { Interceptor } from './interceptor'; import type { LlmLogEntry } from './options';`. NEVER add a new export to src/index.ts.

finding.finding: (1) `capturePayloads: true` needed for body assertions (default off). (2) Emission deferred via setImmediate; await TWO ticks before asserting. (3) Patch targets http.ClientRequest.prototype; under Jest it still works. (4) `callerTrace` resolves to 'unknown' under Jest — do NOT assert. (5) `inputTokens` may be 0 for empty messages arrays — assert >= 0. (6) Gemini key travels as `?key=` on the URL — must assert `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` excludes the key value. (7) Default redaction masks `api_key`/`authorization` body keys but NOT URL query params — Gemini URL-key safety is the test's responsibility.
finding.implication: Add header comments documenting two-setImmediate flush, capturePayloads default-off, callerTrace 'unknown' allowance. For Gemini, hard-assert `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` excludes the key value (read into a local variable, never hardcoded).

requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Obtain from Anthropic Console (https://console.anthropic.com/) > Settings > API Keys. Set as a shell env var only at the moment of opt-in test invocation. Never hardcoded, never committed, never written to a fixture file.

requiredMaterials.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
requiredMaterials.whyNeeded: Required to execute packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts in opt-in mode and verify the interceptor captures a real OpenAI Chat Completions call end-to-end. Without it, the suite resolves to describe.skip.
requiredMaterials.acquisitionNote: Obtain from OpenAI Platform (https://platform.openai.com/) > API Keys > Create new secret key. Set as a shell env var only at the moment of opt-in test invocation. Never hardcoded, never committed, never written to a fixture file.

requiredMaterials.name: GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback)

phases.name: Add fetch baseline integration test
phases.goal: Add a non-provider, always-on raw fetch smoke test that proves the in-process interceptor captures a real HTTPS request end-to-end, gated so the default `npm test` skips it instantly and without credentials.
phases.rationale: The fetch baseline is the simplest live smoke test and exercises a capability none of the three LLM-provider tests can stand in for: raw HTTPS interception without provider-specific request/response shape. If a future regression broke plain-HTTPS interception but kept the LLM-specific path working (a host-filter bypass, a parseCall failure outside the LLM response grammar), only this baseline would catch it. Gated so it skips under `npm test` but runs when invoked directly.
changes: Create packages/llm-http-proxy/src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts that imports `{ Interceptor }` from './interceptor' and `type { LlmLogEntry }` from './options', defines a named suite function that builds an Interceptor with providers set to a regex matching a public HTTPS host (e.g. /example\.com/) and a logger that pushes emitted entries into a local array, fires one global fetch() POST against https://example.com/ with a tiny JSON body, awaits two setImmediate() ticks after response-end, then asserts entries.length === 1, that entries[0].url contains 'example.com', entries[0].model is a string, and JSON.stringify(entries[0]) is non-empty.

Wrap the suite in the same `if (gate) { describe(...) } else { describe.skip(...) }` shape as src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366, where the gate is computed via `process.env.npm_lifecycle_event !== 'test'` so the suite runs whenever the file is invoked directly (e.g. `npx jest src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts`) and resolves to describe.skip under `npm test`.

Add a header comment documenting that the file is opt-in with no API key, that it is gated by direct jest invocation (npm sets npm_lifecycle_event='test' only when running `npm test`), and that the two-setImmediate flush pattern is required because emission is deferred via setImmediate — explain this for a future maintainer.
inputs: RUN_BENCH gate shape from src/benchmark.test.ts lines 317 and 359-366
withEntries / install-restore / two-setImmediate flush pattern from src/interceptor.test.ts lines 75-91
fetch availability on Node >=18 from package.json engines.node (verified by discovery finding fetch-availability)
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts exists, passes one test when invoked via `npx jest src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts` against the real https://example.com/ endpoint, and resolves to describe.skip under default `npm test` (verified by running `npm test` and observing zero added tests and zero network egress).

rubric.label: Test file exists at the declared path with required imports
rubric.ruleStatement: The new integration test file must exist at exactly packages/llm-http-proxy/src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts and import Interceptor and the LlmLogEntry type from the right modules.
passCriteria: A file is present at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts
The file contains `import { Interceptor } from './interceptor'`
The file contains `import type { LlmLogEntry } from './options'`
failureExamples: File is missing entirely from packages/llm-http-proxy/src/
File is named fetch-baseline.test.ts (no `.integration.` infix)
Import statement reads from a wrong relative path such as '../interceptor'

rubric.label: Suite resolves to describe.skip under default npm test with zero network egress
rubric.ruleStatement: Running `npm test` from the package root must not execute the suite — it must short-circuit to describe.skip, produce no outbound HTTPS traffic to example.com, and add zero test results to the default report.
passCriteria: The suite body is wrapped in `if (gate) { describe(...) } else { describe.skip(...) }` matching the shape used at src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366
The `gate` value is derived from process.env (not hardcoded true/false) so it can flip based on invocation context
Running `npm test` from packages/llm-http-proxy completes with no captured DNS lookup or TCP connection to example.com
The jest output for the default run shows the suite as skipped (or entirely absent from the discovered-tests count)
failureExamples: Gate is omitted and the suite runs unconditionally, causing `npm test` to attempt a real fetch and either fail offline or add latency
Gate uses `process.env.CI` (always falsy locally) so the test still runs under `npm test`
Gate is `describe.skip` with no opt-in branch — file is dead code and cannot be run at all

rubric.label: Direct jest invocation fires a real fetch and asserts the interceptor captured the entry
rubric.ruleStatement: When the file is invoked directly (e.g. via `npx jest src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts`), the test must perform one real HTTPS POST against https://example.com/, flush deferred emission with two setImmediate() ticks, and assert the captured entry has the expected shape.
passCriteria: The test calls global `fetch()` exactly once with URL `https://example.com/` and a small JSON body
The test awaits two `setImmediate()` ticks after the response settles before reading the captured entries array
The test asserts `entries.length === 1`
The test asserts `entries[0].url` contains the substring `example.com`
The test asserts `typeof entries[0].model === 'string'`
The test asserts `JSON.stringify(entries[0]).length > 0`
failureExamples: Test mocks fetch instead of calling the real endpoint
Test points at http://localhost:3000 — proves nothing about real HTTPS interception
Test omits the setImmediate flush — entries.length is 0 and the suite flakes
Test only checks entries.length and skips the url/model/JSON.stringify assertions

rubric.label: No API keys or credential lookups appear in the file
rubric.ruleStatement: The fetch baseline is the only smoke test in the live-provider suite that must execute without any provider credential. The file must contain no environment lookups for *_API_KEY and no hardcoded secrets — its whole purpose is to prove interception works on a public host with no auth.
passCriteria: The file source contains no read of process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, or any other *_API_KEY variable
The file source contains no string literal resembling a key prefix (e.g. `sk-`, `key-`) longer than 8 chars
The header comment explicitly states the suite requires no API key
failureExamples: File reads process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY left over from copy-pasting another test template
File hardcodes a placeholder key string for `Authorization` header
Header comment says 'requires OPENAI_API_KEY to be set' contradicting the no-credentials goal

rubric.label: Interceptor is installed and reliably restored so global fetch is not leaked
rubric.ruleStatement: The suite must install the Interceptor before the fetch call and guarantee restoration of the original global fetch afterward — a regression here would silently corrupt every other test in the package that touches global fetch.
passCriteria: An `Interceptor` instance is constructed with a `providers` option whose regex matches /example\.com/
The interceptor is given a `logger` option whose implementation pushes each emitted entry into a local array
The test installs the interceptor (either via a `withEntries` helper or a try/finally block) before the fetch call
The original global fetch is restored in a finally / afterEach so a thrown assertion does not leave the suite's monkey-patch in place
failureExamples: Interceptor is built but never installed — entries array stays empty and the suite falsely fails
Interceptor is installed but never uninstalled — global fetch stays patched and breaks downstream unit tests
Restoration lives after the assertion but outside a try/finally — a failed assertion leaks the patch

rubric.label: Header comment explains the opt-in gate and the setImmediate flush
rubric.ruleStatement: A header comment at the top of the suite must explain why the suite is opt-in, how the gate distinguishes `npm test` from direct invocation, and why two setImmediate() ticks are awaited — so a future maintainer does not delete the gate thinking it is dead code or remove the flush thinking it is superstition.
passCriteria: A comment block appears above the suite describing the file as opt-in
The comment explains the gate mechanism in terms of `npm_lifecycle_event` or equivalent (or whatever env signal the implementation chose)
The comment explains that the two setImmediate() awaits are required because emission is deferred via setImmediate
failureExamples: No header comment — a future maintainer removes the gate thinking it is unused scaffolding and the suite runs in CI
Comment explains opt-in but not setImmediate — a future maintainer removes the flush and the test starts flaking on slow machines
Comment only says `// integration test` with no operational instructions

phases.healerHint: If the gate resolves to skip under direct invocation (or to run under `npm test`), replace the `npm_lifecycle_event` check with a positive opt-in env var like `RUN_FETCH_BASELINE=1` and invoke the file via `RUN_FETCH_BASELINE=1 npx jest src/fetch-baseline.integration.test.ts` — the proven RUN_BENCH pattern in src/benchmark.test.ts is the template to mirror.

phases.name: Add Anthropic integration test
phases.goal: Add a real Anthropic Messages API smoke test gated on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY presence (no separate LIVE flag), asserting the interceptor captures a model + url + non-zero token counts from a live minimal completion call, with a defense-in-depth no-key-leak assertion.
phases.rationale: Anthropic uses header-based auth (`x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`) — the simplest provider to integrate after the fetch baseline — so its smoke test is the natural second phase. It must include a defense-in-depth `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does-not-contain-the-key assertion even though headers do not normally leak into LlmLogEntry; future redaction changes could regress this.
changes: Create packages/llm-http-proxy/src/anthropic.integration.test.ts that imports `{ Interceptor }` from './interceptor' and `type { LlmLogEntry }` from './options', reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` into a local `apiKey` variable (typed as `string | undefined`; treat empty string the same as unset), and gates the suite on `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0` so the suite resolves to `describe.skip('anthropic live (skip: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set)')` when the key is missing — there is no separate LIVE flag; the API key IS the opt-in.

Define a named suite function that builds an Interceptor with `providers: ['api.anthropic.com']` and a logger pushing entries into a local array, fires one real `https.request` POST to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with body `{"model":"claude-3-5-haiku-20241022","max_tokens":1,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}` and headers `x-api-key: <apiKey>`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `content-type: application/json`; awaits two setImmediate() ticks after response-end.

Assert entries.length === 1, entries[0].url contains 'api.anthropic.com/v1/messages', entries[0].model contains 'claude', entries[0].inputTokens >= 0, entries[0].outputTokens >= 0, and that `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does NOT include the literal value of `apiKey` (defense-in-depth).

Wrap the suite in `if (apiKey) { describe('anthropic live', suite) } else { describe.skip('anthropic live (skip: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set)', () => {}) }` (using the same if/else describe|describe.skip shape as src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366, just gated on the key instead of a LIVE flag) and add a header comment explaining the gate, the two-setImmediate flush, the callerTrace 'unknown' allowance under Jest, and why capturePayloads stays default-off.
inputs: RUN_BENCH gate shape from src/benchmark.test.ts lines 317 and 359-366 (template for the if/else describe wrapper)
withEntries / install-restore / two-setImmediate flush pattern from src/interceptor.test.ts lines 75-91
LlmLogEntry shape from src/options.ts lines 18-31 (asserted fields: model, url, inputTokens, outputTokens)
Anthropic minimal request shape from discovery finding provider-request-shape-minimums (POST /v1/messages with x-api-key + anthropic-version headers, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 model, max_tokens=1)
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/anthropic.integration.test.ts exists, passes one test when invoked via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... npx jest src/anthropic.integration.test.ts`, and resolves to describe.skip under default `npm test` AND when invoked without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the env.

rubric.label: Opt-in gate keyed solely on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY presence
rubric.ruleStatement: The test suite must skip when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset and run only when it is set; there must be no separate LIVE/RUN_X flag — key presence IS the opt-in (the rubric guards the RUN_BENCH-template convention referenced in src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366).
passCriteria: Open the new file and locate the top-level describe: it must be wrapped in `if (apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0) { describe('anthropic live', suite) } else { describe.skip('anthropic live (skip: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set)', ...) }` — the gate is the key, not RUN_LIVE or any second flag.
Grep the file for `RUN_LIVE`, `LIVE=`, `INTEGRATION=`, and any second `process.env`: only one process.env reference exists and it reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; no second opt-in flag is declared.

Run `npx jest src/anthropic.integration.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E 'skip|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'`: with the env var unset the output shows the `skip: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set` reason with zero passing tests; with it set the same command shows the live suite name and one test result.
failureExamples: File gates on both `process.env.LIVE === '1'` AND `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — adds a redundant second opt-in flag contrary to the RUN_BENCH template.

File uses `if (!apiKey) return;` at the top of a plain `describe` — registers the suite unconditionally rather than via `describe.skip`, so under default `npm test` Jest reports the suite as 'passed' with zero assertions and the absence of the gate is masked.
File reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY but never references `apiKey.length`; an export of empty-string still attempts the live call and fails noisily in CI.

rubric.label: API key sourced only from env, typed string | undefined, empty treated as unset
rubric.ruleStatement: The key must come from process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (never a literal, fixture, or config file); the local variable must be typed string | undefined so the unset-handling branch is type-checked; an empty-string env var must be treated as missing.
passCriteria: The literal `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` appears exactly once in the file and only as `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, assigned to a local variable named `apiKey`.
The assignment to `apiKey` carries the type `string | undefined` (an explicit `: string | undefined` annotation) so the empty-string branch in the gate is required to compile, not optional.
Grep the file for hardcoded key fragments, `dotenv`, `fs.readFileSync`, or a second env var holding credential material: none of these appear.
failureExamples: Test file hardcodes `const apiKey = 'sk-ant-test-...'` — leaks the test fixture into the diff history and would be flagged in code review for storing a credential in source.

Test types `const apiKey: string = process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — under strict mode and a clean checkout `apiKey` is `undefined` and the gate compiles only by accident, so the skip path is never exercised.

Test reads `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY || 'placeholder'` — empty-string env vars substitute a placeholder and the live call fires against Anthropic with an invalid key, hitting 401 instead of skipping.

rubric.label: One real POST to api.anthropic.com/v1/messages with documented headers and body
rubric.ruleStatement: Exactly one live HTTPS request must fire, targeting the Messages endpoint with the canonical Anthropic auth headers and a minimal payload that returns quickly and cheaply.
passCriteria: Locate the request block: it is a single `https.request(...)` (or `fetch`) POST to `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` and no other host appears anywhere in the file.
Request headers set `x-api-key: <apiKey>`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, and `content-type: application/json`; the casing of these header names matches exactly.
Request body contains `model: 'claude-3-5-haiku-20241022'`, `max_tokens: 1`, and `messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }]`; there is no `stream: true`, no `tools:` block, and no `system:` prompt.
The Interceptor constructor in the file passes `providers: ['api.anthropic.com']` and this is the only provider in the array.
failureExamples: Request targets `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete` (legacy endpoint) — Anthropic returns 404 and the test fails for the wrong reason, polluting signals about interceptor behavior.
Body omits `max_tokens` — Anthropic issues a free-form completion that can consume unbounded tokens, tripping a billing alarm during a smoke test.
Headers use `Authorization: Bearer <key>` instead of `x-api-key` — Anthropic returns 401 and the test gives a false-negative signal about the interceptor itself.
Interceptor constructed with `providers: ['*']` or an empty array — captures no entries and `entries.length === 1` fails even on a successful network call.

rubric.label: Assertions cover entry count, URL, model, and non-negative token counts
rubric.ruleStatement: After the request completes, the test must prove the interceptor captured a single, well-formed entry — counting entries, asserting URL contains the Messages path, asserting model contains 'claude', and asserting inputTokens and outputTokens are non-negative.
passCriteria: Inside the live describe block, `expect(entries.length).toBe(1)` appears exactly once.
`expect(entries[0].url).toContain('api.anthropic.com/v1/messages')` and `expect(entries[0].model).toContain('claude')` both appear in the file (or equivalent `toMatch(/claude/)`).
`expect(entries[0].inputTokens).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` and `expect(entries[0].outputTokens).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` both appear in the file.
failureExamples: Test asserts `entries.length > 0` — passes if two entries land and the test was supposed to prove exactly one capture, so a regression in capture-de-dup logic slips through.
Model assertion uses `toBe('claude-3-5-haiku-20241022')` (exact match); brittle against Anthropic deprecating or renaming the model; should be `toContain('claude')`.

Token assertion uses `toBeGreaterThan(0)` — Anthropic may legitimately round-trip `output_tokens: 0` on a `max_tokens:1` empty-completion branch; the test passes only on the happy path and fails noisily otherwise.

rubric.label: Defense-in-depth assertion that the captured entry does not contain the API key
rubric.ruleStatement: Even though Anthropic uses header-based auth, a regression in redaction logic could cause the key to appear in a captured field; the test must guard with an explicit negative assertion that JSON.stringify(entries[0]) does NOT contain the literal apiKey value.
passCriteria: Find the negative assertion in the file: it uses `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` (not `entries[0].url`, not `entries[0].headers`) so the check covers every captured field.
The assertion is in negative form (`expect(...).not.toContain(apiKey)` or `.not.toMatch(apiKey)`) and the operand is the literal `apiKey` variable, not a hardcoded prefix.

Grep the file for any other reference to `apiKey` outside the env-var read site and the header/assertion sites: only those two usages exist; nothing logs the key, prints it, or interpolates it into an error message.
failureExamples: Assertion is `expect(JSON.stringify(entries[0])).not.toContain('sk-ant-')` — prefix check passes even if redaction accidentally includes a suffixed key fragment; the operand must be the full literal `apiKey`.
Assertion checks only `entries[0].request.headers` — headers are not part of LlmLogEntry today, so this is a no-op and gives false confidence.
Test contains `console.log('using key', apiKey)` for debugging — leaks the key on every CI run that exports the variable.

rubric.label: Two setImmediate() ticks after response-end and an install/restore wrapper
rubric.ruleStatement: The interceptor flushes captured entries on a setImmediate tick after the response ends (per src/interceptor.test.ts lines 75-91); the test must await two ticks before asserting and must install/restore the interceptor so the global state changes do not leak into other tests in the package.
passCriteria: After the response `'end'` handler in the file, two `await new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve))` calls appear in sequence — the count is exactly two, not one, not three.

The file uses `beforeEach`/`afterEach` (or a paired `beforeAll`/`afterAll`) that call the Interceptor's install and restore methods, and the import statement `import { Interceptor } from './interceptor'` is present.

The header comment at the top of the file explains why two ticks are required (capture flushed async after response-end) and names a source file (e.g., src/interceptor.test.ts or src/interceptor.ts) so the pattern is traceable.
failureExamples: Test awaits one `setImmediate` only — race: assertion runs before the entry lands in the array, `entries.length === 0`, producing a flaky failure on slow CI.
Test fires the request but never installs the Interceptor — the request still succeeds but `entries` stays empty and `entries.length === 1` fails for a reason unrelated to interceptor behavior.
Test installs but never restores — subsequent unit tests in the package see interceptors on their HTTP requests and produce noise or false failures that hide the real regression.

phases.healerHint: Most likely failure is a flaky `entries` array that is empty when the assertion runs; fix by buffering the body, awaiting `new Promise(resolve => response.on('end', resolve))` and then awaiting `new Promise(resolve => setImmediate(resolve))` twice before any assertion, mirroring the withEntries/install-restore pattern at src/interceptor.test.ts:75-91.

phases.name: Add OpenAI integration test
phases.goal: Add a real OpenAI Chat Completions smoke test gated on OPENAI_API_KEY presence (no separate LIVE flag), asserting the interceptor captures a model + url + non-zero token counts from a live minimal completion call, with a defense-in-depth no-key-leak assertion.
phases.rationale: OpenAI also uses header-based auth (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`) — structurally the same as Anthropic but on a different host and request body, so it gets its own file (one provider per phase) and mirrors the Anthropic gate/assertion shape. Splitting into its own phase keeps each file under one deliverable and keeps provider-specific request bodies from cross-contaminating.
changes: Create packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts that imports `{ Interceptor }` from './interceptor' and `type { LlmLogEntry }` from './options', reads `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` into a local `apiKey` variable (typed as `string | undefined`; treat empty string the same as unset), and gates the suite on `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0` so the suite resolves to `describe.skip('openai live (skip: OPENAI_API_KEY not set)')` when the key is missing — there is no separate LIVE flag; the API key IS the opt-in.

Define a named suite function that builds an Interceptor with `providers: ['api.openai.com']` and a logger pushing entries into a local array, fires one real `https.request` POST to `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with body `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":1,"stream":false}` and header `authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` plus `content-type: application/json`; awaits two setImmediate() ticks after response-end.

Assert entries.length === 1, entries[0].url contains 'api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions', entries[0].model contains 'gpt', entries[0].inputTokens >= 0, entries[0].outputTokens >= 0, and that `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does NOT include the literal value of `apiKey` (defense-in-depth).

Wrap the suite in `if (apiKey) { describe('openai live', suite) } else { describe.skip('openai live (skip: OPENAI_API_KEY not set)', () => {}) }` (using the same if/else describe|describe.skip shape as src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366, just gated on the key instead of a LIVE flag) and add a header comment explaining the gate, the two-setImmediate flush, the callerTrace 'unknown' allowance under Jest, and why capturePayloads stays default-off.
inputs: RUN_BENCH gate shape from src/benchmark.test.ts lines 317 and 359-366
withEntries / install-restore / two-setImmediate flush pattern from src/interceptor.test.ts lines 75-91
OpenAI minimal request shape from discovery finding provider-request-shape-minimums (POST /v1/chat/completions with Authorization Bearer header, gpt-4o-mini model, max_tokens=1, stream=false)
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts exists, passes one test when invoked via `OPENAI_API_KEY=... npx jest src/openai.integration.test.ts`, and resolves to describe.skip under default `npm test` AND when invoked without OPENAI_API_KEY in the env.

rubric.label: File exists at the documented path with the documented imports
rubric.ruleStatement: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts must exist and import the Interceptor class from './interceptor' plus the LlmLogEntry type from './options', so the deliverable is wired to the package's own production surface and not a parallel re-implementation.
passCriteria: A file is present at packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts relative to the repo root.
The file contains an import statement that brings in the named binding Interceptor from the relative module './interceptor'.
The file contains an import statement that brings in the type-only binding LlmLogEntry from the relative module './options'.

The file opens with a comment block that names the OPENAI_API_KEY gate, the two-setImmediate flush, the callerTrace 'unknown' allowance under Jest, and the rationale for leaving capturePayloads at its default (off).
failureExamples: The file is created at src/__tests__/openai.integration.test.ts or any path other than packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts.
The file imports from a deep path like '../src/interceptor' instead of the relative './interceptor' the package's own source uses.
The file omits the LlmLogEntry type import and uses `any` for the entries array.
The header comment is missing or mentions a separate LIVE flag that does not exist in the code.

rubric.label: Gate is OPENAI_API_KEY presence alone (no separate LIVE flag) and flips describe/describe.skip correctly
rubric.ruleStatement: The suite must opt in solely on OPENAI_API_KEY being present (treating an empty string the same as unset) and must resolve to describe.skip under the default `npm test`, so CI never hits api.openai.com without credentials.
passCriteria: A top-level `const apiKey = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` (or `let apiKey: string | undefined = process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY`) is declared at module scope; the type is `string | undefined`, not `string`.
An empty-string check is applied so `apiKey === ''` is treated the same as undefined (e.g. `apiKey && apiKey.length > 0` or equivalent guard).
There is no `process.env.LIVE`, `process.env.RUN_LIVE`, or similar second gate variable anywhere in the file.

The suite is wrapped in `if (apiKey) { describe('openai live', suiteFn) } else { describe.skip('openai live (skip: OPENAI_API_KEY not set)', () => {}) }` matching the shape in src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366 (gated on the key instead of RUN_BENCH).

Running `unset OPENAI_API_KEY && npx jest packages/llm-http-proxy/src/openai.integration.test.ts` produces a report whose only entry is the skipped `openai live (skip: ...)` line and zero network attempts.
failureExamples: apiKey is typed as `string` and the test crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` when the env var is missing.
The file checks `process.env.LIVE === '1' && process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` — the LIVE flag contradicts the phase rule that the key IS the opt-in.
The describe.skip branch is omitted entirely, so `npm test` in CI fires a real request to api.openai.com and either hangs, errors with 401, or incurs cost.
The skip label says `(skip: no key)` but the gate reads `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` directly inside `it(...)`, so the test still runs and the label lies.

rubric.label: HTTP request shape matches the documented OpenAI minimums
rubric.ruleStatement: The live request must hit api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with the documented body and Authorization Bearer header, so the captured entry's url and model are actually populated by the OpenAI server (not by some accidental other host).
passCriteria: The request URL string contains `api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`.
The request method is POST (the code uses `https.request(..., { method: 'POST', hostname: 'api.openai.com', ... })` or builds an equivalent POST).
An `authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` request header is set before `req.end(...)`.
A `content-type: application/json` request header is set before `req.end(...)`.

The request body JSON string equals `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":1,"stream":false}` (whitespace and key order may vary, but the four fields — model, messages, max_tokens, stream — must all be present with these values).
failureExamples: The host is hard-coded as `api.openai.com` but the path is `/v1/completions` (legacy) or `/v1/responses` (new endpoint), so the request returns 404 and the test never sees the captured entry.
The header is `Authorization: <apiKey>` without the `Bearer ` prefix, so OpenAI rejects with 401 and `entries` stays empty.
The body sets `max_tokens: 1` but leaves out `stream: false`, so OpenAI streams the response and the test never sees a `response` callback that carries usage tokens.
The body uses `model: 'gpt-4'` instead of `gpt-4o-mini`, which inflates cost and contradicts the documented minimums.

rubric.label: Interceptor captures url + model + non-negative token counts from one live call
rubric.ruleStatement: After the live call, the in-process interceptor must yield exactly one captured LlmLogEntry whose url, model, inputTokens, and outputTokens satisfy the documented assertions — proving interception fires on a real OpenAI response, not just on a mocked one.
passCriteria: An `Interceptor` instance is constructed with `providers: ['api.openai.com']` (and no other provider that would absorb this host).
A logger callback is passed that appends each captured entry to a local `entries: LlmLogEntry[]` array.
The test awaits two `setImmediate()` ticks (or one `setImmediate` plus one `process.nextTick`, equivalent) AFTER the response `end` event before asserting, so the logger's microtask has flushed.
`expect(entries.length).toBe(1)` is asserted.
`expect(entries[0].url).toContain('api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions')` is asserted.
`expect(entries[0].model).toContain('gpt')` (or `toMatch(/gpt/)`) is asserted.
`expect(entries[0].inputTokens).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` and `expect(entries[0].outputTokens).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)` are asserted.
failureExamples: The test fires the request and immediately asserts — the logger callback hasn't run yet, `entries.length === 0`, and the suite reports a false failure.
The Interceptor is constructed with `providers: ['openai.com']` (missing the `api.` subdomain) so the request bypasses interception and `entries` stays empty.
The model assertion is `toBe('gpt-4o-mini')` (exact match); if OpenAI ever returns `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` the test fails for the wrong reason.
Token assertions use `toBe(1)` instead of `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0)`, so any response whose usage is reported as `completion_tokens: 0` (the `max_tokens: 1` minimum) fails.

rubric.label: Defense-in-depth: captured log entry does not contain the API key
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must assert that `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does NOT include the literal apiKey value, so a future regression that accidentally echoes the credential into a log entry is caught at test time.
passCriteria: The apiKey value is read into a local variable before the assertion, not interpolated from `process.env` inside the assertion string.
An explicit assertion of the form `expect(JSON.stringify(entries[0])).not.toContain(apiKey)` is present in the test body.
The assertion runs against `entries[0]` specifically (the entry produced by the live call), not against `entries` as a whole, so a leaked key from a future multi-call test would still surface.
The apiKey used in the assertion is the same variable that was sent in the `authorization` header — not a re-read of `process.env`.
failureExamples: The assertion is missing entirely; the captured entry happens to be safe today but nothing prevents a regression.
The assertion checks `not.toContain(process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY!)` instead of the local `apiKey` variable, which TypeScript-strict lints will reject and which obscures the dependency.
The assertion is `expect(entries[0].headers?.authorization).not.toContain(apiKey)`, which only protects one field — a leak into `body` or `error` would slip past.
The apiKey value is a truncated form (`apiKey.slice(0, 8)`) so a partial leak doesn't fail the test.

phases.healerHint: If the suite reports `entries.length === 0` against a real key, the logger hasn't flushed yet — add the two `setImmediate()` ticks after the response `end` handler so the assertion runs after the interceptor's microtask.

phases.name: Add Gemini integration test
phases.goal: Add a real Google generative-language API smoke test gated on GEMINI_API_KEY presence (no separate LIVE flag), asserting the interceptor captures model + url + non-zero token counts from a live minimal completion call, with the load-bearing URL-key safety check because Gemini transmits the key as a URL query parameter.
phases.rationale: Gemini is the only provider in this set that transmits the API key on the wire as a URL query parameter (`?key=...`), which discovery's gotchas item #6 and the materials flag as the load-bearing safety check. This phase therefore carries the strongest defense-in-depth assertion and gets its own file so the URL-key safety logic is not diluted across the other providers.
changes: Create packages/llm-http-proxy/src/gemini.integration.test.ts that imports `{ Interceptor }` from './interceptor' and `type { LlmLogEntry }` from './options', reads `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY` (with fallback to `process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY` if the canonical one is unset, documented in the header comment) into a local `apiKey` variable (typed as `string | undefined`; treat empty string the same as unset), and gates the suite on `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0` so the suite resolves to `describe.skip('gemini live (skip: GEMINI_API_KEY not set)')` when neither key is set — there is no separate LIVE flag; the API key IS the opt-in.

Define a named suite function that builds an Interceptor with `providers: [/generativelanguage\.googleapis\.com/]` and a logger pushing entries into a local array, fires one real `https.request` POST to `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent?key=<apiKey>` with body `{"contents":[{"parts":[{"text":"hi"}]}]}` and header `content-type: application/json`; awaits two setImmediate() ticks after response-end.

Assert entries.length === 1, entries[0].url contains 'generativelanguage.googleapis.com', entries[0].url does NOT include the literal value of `apiKey` (URL-key safety check — the interceptor stores the request path including query string), entries[0].model contains 'gemini', entries[0].inputTokens >= 0, entries[0].outputTokens >= 0, and that `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does NOT include the literal value of `apiKey` (defense-in-depth across all serialized fields).

Wrap the suite in `if (apiKey) { describe('gemini live', suite) } else { describe.skip('gemini live (skip: GEMINI_API_KEY not set)', () => {}) }` (using the same if/else describe|describe.skip shape as src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366, just gated on the key instead of a LIVE flag) and add a header comment explaining the gate, the URL-key safety rationale (Gemini's `?key=` query param means the secret travels on the wire as part of the URL path), the two-setImmediate flush, the callerTrace 'unknown' allowance under Jest, and why capturePayloads stays default-off.
inputs: RUN_BENCH gate shape from src/benchmark.test.ts lines 317 and 359-366
withEntries / install-restore / two-setImmediate flush pattern from src/interceptor.test.ts lines 75-91

Gemini minimal request shape + URL-key safety gotcha from discovery findings provider-request-shape-minimums and gotchas item #6 (POST with `?key=` query param; the interceptor stores the request path including query string, so the key DOES appear on the wire path and the test must assert against the captured entry's serialized form)
phases.expectedResult: packages/llm-http-proxy/src/gemini.integration.test.ts exists, passes one test when invoked via `GEMINI_API_KEY=... npx jest src/gemini.integration.test.ts` (asserting the URL-key safety check holds end-to-end), and resolves to describe.skip under default `npm test` AND when invoked without GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY in the env.

rubric.label: URL-key safety check holds end-to-end
rubric.ruleStatement: Because Gemini transmits the API key on the wire as a URL query parameter (`?key=...`), the captured entry's url field AND its full JSON-serialized form must both be asserted to NOT contain the literal runtime apiKey value — this is the load-bearing safety check for the entire phase and the reason this file gets its own suite.
passCriteria: Run `GEMINI_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) npx jest src/gemini.integration.test.ts` and the test passes (proves the check holds against a non-trivial key, not just an obvious literal).
Grep `gemini.integration.test.ts` for a line that asserts `entries[0].url` does NOT contain the runtime `apiKey` variable (e.g. `not.toContain(apiKey)` against `.url`).
Grep the same file for a line that asserts `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` does NOT contain the runtime `apiKey` variable — the defense-in-depth check across every serialized field.
Both assertions reference the `apiKey` variable (not the string `'GEMINI_API_KEY'` and not `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY` literally substituted).
failureExamples: Only `entries.length === 1` and a model/url substring are asserted; the safety check is missing entirely.

The safety assertion hardcodes `expect(url).not.toContain(process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY!)` — works at runtime but couples the assertion to env-var name lookup instead of the local variable, and breaks under the GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback.
Defense-in-depth `JSON.stringify` check is omitted; only the `.url` substring is checked.
The assertion uses `expect(url).not.toMatch(/key=/)` instead of the literal value — too loose, misses keys that don't follow `key=`.
The check is gated behind a `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY` truthy test that is false under GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback, so the test runs without any safety assertion.

rubric.label: Default `npm test` stays fast and network-free
rubric.ruleStatement: With neither GEMINI_API_KEY nor GOOGLE_API_KEY set in the environment, the file must resolve to `describe.skip` so the default test suite never makes a live network call and never costs more than module-load time.
passCriteria: Run `unset GEMINI_API_KEY GOOGLE_API_KEY && npx jest src/gemini.integration.test.ts` and confirm Jest reports the suite as `skipped`, not `failed` and not `pending` (Jest output shows the skip reason `(skip: GEMINI_API_KEY not set)`).

Run `npm test` from the package root with no live-provider env vars and confirm no network egress to `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (e.g. via a packet sniff or by confirming Jest finishes in under 1s and never opens a TLS handshake).
The source contains an `else { describe.skip(...) }` branch reachable when the key is absent — not just an `it.skip` inside a live `describe` block.
There is NO separate LIVE-flag env var (`RUN_LIVE`, `LIVE=1`, `INTEGRATION=1`, etc.) — the presence of the API key itself is the only opt-in gate.
failureExamples: Suite always runs; `describe.skip` branch is missing or unreachable.
Suite uses `describe('gemini live', () => { if (apiKey) it(...) else it.skip(...) })` — still costs Jest startup and module-load side effects even when skipped.
Suite is gated on `LIVE=1` in addition to (or instead of) the key; passing the key alone does not opt in.
The `else` branch is absent; the file calls `describe` unconditionally and relies on an `it.skip` inside, which still registers the suite as runnable.

rubric.label: Interceptor captures expected Gemini fields from the live response
rubric.ruleStatement: When run with a valid key, exactly one log entry is produced from the single live POST, and that entry carries the fields a junior developer can recognize as a Gemini capture: a host-matching url, a model substring, and non-negative token counts.
passCriteria: The source asserts `entries.length === 1` (exactly one captured request, not zero, not two).
The source asserts `entries[0].url` contains the literal substring `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`.

The source asserts `entries[0].model` contains the substring `gemini` (a `.toLowerCase().includes('gemini')` is acceptable; an exact-match on `gemini-2.0-flash` is NOT acceptable because providers may normalize the model string).
The source asserts `entries[0].inputTokens >= 0` AND `entries[0].outputTokens >= 0` (a trivial `hi` prompt can legitimately yield 0 tokens for either side).
failureExamples: No `entries.length` assertion — the test would pass even if the interceptor silently captured nothing.
Token assertion uses `> 0` instead of `>= 0`; a free-tier trivial prompt legitimately returns 0 input tokens and fails the test spuriously.
Model assertion is `expect(entries[0].model).toBe('gemini-2.0-flash')` — too strict; the provider may normalize or return `models/gemini-2.0-flash`.
The test fires two requests but asserts only one entry — masking a capture-regression.
Assertions read `entries[0]` without first confirming length, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` instead of a clean assertion failure.

rubric.label: GOOGLE_API_KEY fallback is honored and empty-string treated as unset
rubric.ruleStatement: The test must accept either `GEMINI_API_KEY` (canonical) or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` (alias) as the opt-in credential, must prefer the canonical name when both are set, and must treat an empty-string env var identically to an unset one — otherwise CI machines that export `GOOGLE_API_KEY=` as a stub would silently try to hit the live API with an empty key.
passCriteria: The source computes a single `apiKey` variable from `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY ?? process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY` (or equivalent coalescing) — not an `||` chain (which collapses empty string to the next operand, losing the canonical preference when both are set to different non-empty values).
The header comment at the top of the file names `GOOGLE_API_KEY` as the documented fallback.
The gate condition is `apiKey !== undefined && apiKey.length > 0` — an explicit length check, not `if (apiKey)` (which is truthy on non-empty strings but lets `apiKey = ' '` through).
A grep of the file shows ZERO occurrences of `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY` in the gate logic other than as the first operand of the fallback expression — no shadow reads or duplicate gates.
failureExamples: Only reads `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY`, ignores `GOOGLE_API_KEY` entirely.
Uses `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY || process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY` — works for unset but loses preference when both are set.
Uses `if (apiKey)` instead of an explicit length check; a stray empty-string export would still skip, but a single-space value would silently try to call the live API.
Header comment claims fallback support but the code does not implement it.

rubric.label: Gate shape mirrors the RUN_BENCH pattern from src/benchmark.test.ts
rubric.ruleStatement: The opt-in harness must be a single top-level `if (apiKey) { describe('gemini live', suite) } else { describe.skip('gemini live (skip: GEMINI_API_KEY not set)', () => {}) }` — mirroring the if/else describe|describe.skip shape used at src/benchmark.test.ts lines 359-366, so the file's opt-in mechanism is immediately recognizable to anyone who has read the existing benchmark test.
passCriteria: At module top level (outside any describe block), exactly one `if (apiKey) { describe(...) } else { describe.skip(...) }` pair exists.
The live describe label is exactly `'gemini live'` and the skip describe label is exactly `'gemini live (skip: GEMINI_API_KEY not set)'` — a developer can grep for either string and find the suite.
The skip describe body is `() => {}` (empty arrow function), not a `describe.skip(name)` with no second argument (which Jest treats differently across versions).
The gate condition is the same `apiKey` variable used by the fallback dimension — not a re-evaluation of `process.env.*`.
failureExamples: Uses `describe('gemini live', () => { if (apiKey) { it(...) } else { it.skip(...) } })` — wrong shape; still costs Jest describe registration.
Skip label is `'gemini live (skipped)'` or `'skipped: no key'` — inconsistent with the rest of the suite.
Two separate `if` blocks: one for the live describe and one for an unconditional skip — duplicate logic.
Gate condition duplicates `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY || process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY` instead of referencing the already-computed `apiKey` variable.

phases.healerHint: The URL-key safety check is the dimension most likely to fail and most expensive to get wrong — re-read the assertion: it must compare against the runtime `apiKey` variable, not the env-var name, and must be paired with a `JSON.stringify(entries[0])` defense-in-depth assertion; if it ever fails, immediately grep the file for any other string built by interpolating `apiKey` into the captured URL and fix at the variable, not the literal.
